arxiv-1912-08258.title: Xor Filters: Faster and Smaller Than Bloom and Cuckoo Filters Journal: JEA Volume: 1 1 1 1 Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3376122 CCS: Theory of computation Bloom filters and hashing
arxiv-1912-08258.creator: Thomas Mueller Graf, Daniel Lemire
arxiv-1912-08258.description: Abstract . The Bloom filter provides fast approximate set membership while using little memory. Engineers often use these filters to avoid slow operations such as disk or network accesses. As an alternative, a cuckoo filter may need less space than a Bloom filter and it is faster. Chazelle et al.

arxiv-2109-07812.title: Transductive Learning for Unsupervised Text Style Transfer
arxiv-2109-07812.creator: Fei Xiao, Liang Pang, Yanyan Lan, Yan Wang, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng
arxiv-2109-07812.description: Abstract Unsupervised style transfer models are mainly based on an inductive learning approach, which represents the style as embeddings, decoder parameters, or discriminator parameters and directly applies these general rules to the test cases. However, the lacking of parallel corpus hinders the ability of these inductive learning methods on this task.

arxiv-2202-01670.title: Rank Aggregation with Confidence for Large Scale Comparison Data
arxiv-2202-01670.creator: Filipa Valdeira, Cláudia Soares
arxiv-2202-01670.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Filipa Valdeira, Cláudia Soares. In this work, we leverage a generative data model considering comparison noise to develop a fast, precise, and informative ranking algorithm from pairwise comparisons that produces a measure of confidence on each comparison. The problem of ranking a large number of items from noisy and sparse pairwise comparison data arises in diverse applications, like ranking players in online games, document retrieval or ranking human perceptions.

arxiv-2208-13688.title: Using Speech to Reduce Loss of Trust in Humanoid Social Robots*
arxiv-2208-13688.creator: Amandus Krantz, Christian Balkenius, Birger Johansson
arxiv-2208-13688.description: Abstract We present data from two online human-robot interaction experiments where 227 participants viewed videos of a humanoid robot exhibiting faulty or non-faulty behaviours while either remaining mute or speaking. The participants were asked to evaluate their perception of the robot’s trustworthiness, as well as its likeability, animacy, and perceived intelligence.

arxiv-2301-05588.title: Mott insulators with boundary zeros
arxiv-2301-05588.creator: N. Wagner, L. Crippa, A. Amaricci, P. Hansmann, M. Klett, E. J. König, T. Schäfer, D. Di Sante, J. Cano, A. J. Millis, A. Georges, G. Sangiovanni
arxiv-2301-05588.description: Abstract The topological classification of electronic band structures is based on symmetry properties of Bloch eigenstates of single-particle Hamiltonians. In parallel, topological field theory has opened the doors to the formulation and characterization of non-trivial phases of matter driven by strong electron-electron interaction.

arxiv-2303-13794.title: Efficient and Accurate Co-Visible Region Localization with Matching Key-Points Crop (MKPC): A Two-Stage Pipeline for Enhancing Image Matching Performance
arxiv-2303-13794.creator: Hongjian Song*, Yuki Kashiwaba*, Shuai Wu, Canming Wang
arxiv-2303-13794.description: Abstract Image matching is a classic and fundamental task in computer vision. In this paper, under the hypothesis that the areas outside the co-visible regions carry little information, we propose a matching key-points crop (MKPC) algorithm. The MKPC locates, proposes and crops the critical regions, which are the co-visible areas with great efficiency and accuracy.

arxiv-2401-09536.title: Few-body precursors of topological frustration
arxiv-2401-09536.creator: Michele Grossi
arxiv-2401-09536.description: Abstract Quantum spin chains - the prototypical model for coupled two-level systems - offer a fertile playground both for fundamental and technological applications, ranging from the theory of thermalization to quantum computation. The effects of frustration induced by the boundary conditions have recently been addressed in this context.

arxiv-2409-12806.title: Enumeration of weighted quadrant walks: criteria for algebraicity and D-finiteness Thanks: This work has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under the Grant Agreement No. 759702, from Centre Henri Lebesgu
arxiv-2409-12806.creator: Thomas Dreyfus, Andrew Elvey Price, Kilian Raschel
arxiv-2409-12806.description: Abstract . In the field of enumeration of weighted walks confined to the quarter plane, it is known that the generating functions behave very differently depending on the chosen step set; in practice, the techniques used in the literature depend on the complexity of the counting series.

arxiv-2508-10804.title: Non-Stationary Restless Multi-Armed Bandits with Provable Guarantee
arxiv-2508-10804.creator: Yu-Heng Hung, Ping-Chun Hsieh, Kai Wang
arxiv-2508-10804.description: Abstract Online restless multi-armed bandits (RMABs) typically assume that each arm follows a stationary Markov Decision Process (MDP) with fixed state transitions and rewards. However, in real-world applications like healthcare and recommendation systems, these assumptions often break due to non-stationary dynamics, posing significant challenges for traditional RMAB algorithms.

arxiv-2510-02783.title: On unconditionality and higher-order Schreier unconditionality Thanks: This work was partially supported by the College of Arts & Sciences at Texas A&M University.
arxiv-2510-02783.creator: Shiliaev Mark
arxiv-2510-02783.description: Abstract . Let X X be a Banach space, ( e n ) n = 1 ∞ (e_{n})_{n=1}^{\infty} be its basis, and S α S_{\alpha} be a Schreier family of order alpha. We introduce Condition A which is a weaker version of the Continuum Hypothesis.

arxiv-2511-10684.title: SpiderGen:Towards Procedure Generation For Carbon Life Cycle Assessments with Generative AI
arxiv-2511-10684.creator: Anupama Sitaraman, Bharathan Balaji, Yuvraj Agarwal
arxiv-2511-10684.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anupama Sitaraman, Bharathan Balaji, Yuvraj Agarwal. Investigating the effects of climate change and global warming caused by GHG emissions have been a key concern worldwide. These emissions are largely contributed to by the production, use and disposal of consumer products. Thus, it is important to build tools to estimate the environmental impact of consumer goods, an essential part of which is conducting Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs). LCAs specify and account for the appropriate processes involved with the production, use, and disposal of the products.

arxiv-2602-09775.title: Where Do Images Come From? Analyzing Captions to Geographically Profile Datasets
arxiv-2602-09775.creator: Abhipsa Basu, Yugam Bahl, Kirti Bhagat, Preethi Seshadri, R. Venkatesh Babu, Danish Pruthi
arxiv-2602-09775.description: Abstract Recent studies show that text-to-image models often fail to generate geographically representative images, raising concerns about the representativeness of their training data and motivating the question: which parts of the world do these training examples come from? We geographically profile large-scale multimodal datasets by mapping image–caption pairs to countries based on location information extracted from captions using LLMs.

europmc-pmc2841614.title: Emergence of spatial structure in cell groups and the evolution of cooperation.
europmc-pmc2841614.creator: Nadell CD, Foster KR, Xavier JB.
europmc-pmc2841614.description: On its own, a single cell cannot exert more than a microscopic influence on its immediate surroundings. However, via strength in numbers and the expression of cooperative phenotypes, such cells can enormously impact their environments. Simple cooperative phenotypes appear to...

europmc-pmc2929501.title: H2AX Phosphorylation: Its Role in DNA Damage Response and Cancer Therapy.
europmc-pmc2929501.creator: Podhorecka M, Skladanowski A, Bozko P.
europmc-pmc2929501.description: Double-strand breaks (DSBs) are the most deleterious DNA lesions, which, if left unrepaired, may have severe consequences for cell survival, as they lead to chromosome aberrations, genomic instability, or cell death. Various physical, chemical, and biological factors are...

europmc-pmc4367969.title: Future coastal population growth and exposure to sea-level rise and coastal flooding--a global assessment.
europmc-pmc4367969.creator: Neumann B, Vafeidis AT, Zimmermann J, Nicholls RJ.
europmc-pmc4367969.description: Coastal zones are exposed to a range of coastal hazards including sea-level rise with its related effects. At the same time, they are more densely populated than the hinterland and exhibit higher rates of population growth and urbanisation. As this trend is expected to continue...

pmc-10575371.title: A Fast Method for Multidimensional Joint Parameter Estimation of Polarization-Sensitive Arrays
pmc-10575371.creator: Zheqi Zhang, Xiang Lan, Xianpeng Wang
pmc-10575371.description: The paper proposes a fast method for the multidimensional parameter estimation of a polarization-sensitive array. Compared with conventional methods (e.g., MUSIC algorithm), the proposed method applies an iterative approach based on Newton’s method to obtain joint estimation results instead of a spectral search and dimension reduction.

pmc-10705802.title: Effect of Acute and Cumulative Stress on Gene Expression in Mammary Tissue and Their Interactions with Physiological Responses and Milk Yield in Saanen Goats
pmc-10705802.creator: Marta Liliane de Vasconcelos, Priscila dos Santos Silva, Henrique Barbosa Hooper, Giovana Krempel Fonseca Merighe, Sandra Aparecida de Oliveira, João Alberto Negrão
pmc-10705802.description: Simple SummaryDairy goats face a set of stressful challenges during lactation. In our study, we aimed to understand how daily stressors can impact milk production and also how Saanen goats respond to these stressors. Our results showed that acute stress imposed sequentially caused cumulative stress and decreased the milk yield of a stressed goat.

pmc-11510021.title: A Review of Nonhuman Primate Models of Rift Valley Fever Virus Infection: Progress, Challenge Strains, and Future Directions
pmc-11510021.creator: Kimimuepigha Ebisine, Darcy Quist, Stephen Findlay-Wilson, Emma Kennedy, Stuart Dowall
pmc-11510021.description: Rift Valley fever (RVF) is a mosquito-borne viral disease that primarily affects animals, especially ruminants, but has the capacity to infect humans and result in outbreaks. Infection with the causative agent, RVF virus (RVFV), causes severe disease in domestic animals, especially sheep, resulting in fever, anorexia, immobility, abortion, and high morbidity and mortality rates in neonate animals.

pmc-11533673.title: Achievement of pathological complete response with osimertinib for EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma
pmc-11533673.creator: Yasuhiro Fujita, Nobuyuki Take, Shinji Shinohara, Masataka Mori, Masatoshi Kanayama, Masaru Takenaka, Koji Kuroda, Shohei Shimajiri, Fumihiro Tanaka
pmc-11533673.description: BackgroundTyrosine-kinase inhibitors (TKIs) of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) usually provide a potent anti-tumor efficacy with robust radiographic response for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring activating mutations in the EGFR gene. However, first-generation EGFR-TKIs may provide only modest pathological response in the majority of EGFR-mutated NSCLC.

pmc-11587159.title: Efficacy of Anti-CD38 Monoclonal Antibodies for Relapsed or Refractory Multiple Myeloma in Stem Cell Transplant-Ineligible Patients Aged over 65 Years: A Propensity Score-Matched Study
pmc-11587159.creator: Satoshi Yamasaki, Michitoshi Hashiguchi, Nao Yoshida-Sakai, Hiroto Jojima, Koichi Osaki, Takashi Okamura, Yutaka Imamura, Andrei Braester
pmc-11587159.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: The development of newer agents, including anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), has significantly improved overall survival (OS) in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). However, the treatment of older patients with RRMM who are transplant-ineligible remains challenging. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated OS in 78 transplant-ineligible patients with RRMM who were aged ≥ 65 years and treated at our institution between February 2012 and November 2023.

pmc-11655045.title: Quality of Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor Videos Available on TikTok and Bilibili: Content Analysis
pmc-11655045.creator: Zheyu Niu, Yijie Hao, Faji Yang, Qirong Jiang, Yupeng Jiang, Shizhe Zhang, Xie Song, Hong Chang, Xu Zhou, Huaqiang Zhu, Hengjun Gao, Jun Lu, Amaryllis Mavragani
pmc-11655045.description: BackgroundDisseminating disease knowledge through concise videos on various platforms is an innovative and efficient approach. However, it remains uncertain whether pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (pNET)-related videos available on current short video platforms can effectively convey accurate and impactful information to the general public.

pmc-12644453.title: A case report of midodrine to treat protein-losing enteropathy for heart transplant candidacy
pmc-12644453.creator: Sean M Conte, Daniel Tardo, Stephanie Wiltshire, Kavitha Muthiah
pmc-12644453.description: BackgroundProtein-losing enteropathy (PLE) is seen in up to 15% of patients with Fontan circulation and has important nutritional, immunologic, and haemodynamic consequences especially in the context of advanced heart failure. Midodrine, an alpha-1-receptor agonist, increases lymphatic tone, mitigating leak of lymph into the bowel, and has been shown to have clinical and biochemical benefit in patients with Fontan failure.

pmc-12693970.title: Molecular Cloning, Bioinformatics, and Expression Analysis of the NPR1 Homolog in Sesame (Sesamum indicum L.)
pmc-12693970.creator: Mingfeng Yan, Xiaolin Zhao, Xingshen Li, Zhenrui He, Juling Hua, Lingen Wei, Yang Sun, Chuanxu Wan, Shuijin Huang
pmc-12693970.description: Sesame bacterial wilt, caused by the pathogen Ralstonia solanacearum, is a major constraint for continuous cropping. Deciphering the defense mechanisms of sesame is therefore essential to the development of novel and effective control strategies. The Non-expressor of Pathogenesis-Related 1 (NPR1) plays a key role in regulating salicylic acid (SA)-mediated systemic acquired resistance (SAR).

pmc-12706027.title: Optimization of supercritical fluid processes for aripiprazole nanoparticle production using GAS-antisolvent technique and Box-Behnken design
pmc-12706027.creator: Eslam Ansari, Bizhan Honarvar, Seyed Ali Sajadian, Zahra Arab Aboosadi, Mehdi Azizi
pmc-12706027.description: Particle size reduction makes drugs more soluble and bioavailable in the body. Researchers are increasingly interested in supercritical fluid processes for the production of micro- and nanoparticles in pharmaceuticals. In this research, gas anti-solvent (GAS), polyvinyl pyrrolidone polymer (PVP), and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) solvent processes were used for the first time to produce aripiprazole (antipsychotic drug) nanoparticles.

pmc-13104585.title: A protocol for retrospective evaluation of potential patient-level harms of an AI tool for blood culture stewardship
pmc-13104585.creator: Michiel Schinkel, Irene Reijers, Anuschka van der Zaag, Sheena Bhagirath, Lotte Lintmeijer, Liesbeth bij de Vaate, Hazra Moeniralam, Prabath Nanayakkara, Erik Schaftenaar, Hanneke Boon
pmc-13104585.description: Background:Artificial intelligence (AI)-based clinical decision support tools are increasingly developed for diagnostic stewardship, yet their clinical adoption remains limited. A barrier to implementation is concern about potential patient-level harm, particularly when algorithms recommend withholding diagnostic tests that would otherwise be standard practice.

pmc-13174924.title: Approaching Sixfold Chemical Bonding: Metal Dimers MM' Involving Group 4–8 Transition Metals and the Actinides Th–Np. Additive Covalent Radii r6
pmc-13174924.creator: Pekka Pyykkö, Michiko Atsumi
pmc-13174924.description: A set of additive covalent radii is fitted to a combination of experimental data, accurate ab initio computations, and more approximate DFT MM' bond lengths, R, with 12 valence electrons in approximately (1σ)2(2σ)2π4δ4 molecular orbitals. These r6 are typically 10–20 pm shorter than the previous triple‐bond radii r3. Values for the elements Ti–Fe, Zr–Ru, Hf–Os, and Th–Np are fitted.
